label: SITL 40 PX4 reposition no CHANGE_MODE
info: Throwaway probe (delete when §14 records the answer). Fills the empty cell example 30 left: 30 measured PX4 with CHANGE_MODE ON, which is why it accepted. This run is the inverse — CHANGE_MODE OFF, vehicle deliberately not in AUTO_LOITER.

name: PX4 reposition mid-AUTO_TAKEOFF with CHANGE_MODE clear
info:
Flow: Set MIS_TAKEOFF_ALT=40 -> Arm -> Takeoff (default alt, now 40 m) -> 6 s -> Move reposition with changeMode FALSE, while the vehicle is still climbing.

WHY: example 30 retired the 'PX4 needs an OFFBOARD stream' advisory, and that stands. But 30 sent CHANGE_MODE ON, so it says nothing about the flag being clear. PX4 settles into AUTO_LOITER by itself once a takeoff completes — and AUTO_LOITER is exactly the state that satisfies the no-flag path — so the cell cannot be probed from a finished takeoff.

ATTEMPT 1 FAILED, AND THAT IS RECORDED: the first cut of this probe switched to POSCTL to leave Hold. PX4 answered MAV_RESULT_TEMPORARILY_REJECTED (resultCode 1) after 3 retries over 3.0 s, so the reposition never ran and the run correctly scored FAIL — not measured. PX4 refuses POSCTL airborne in this lab, almost certainly for want of an RC link (POSCTL is stick-driven). Example 36 sends the same command to sysid 11 and it ACKs, but on the ground.

ATTEMPT 2 (this flow) needs no mode change at all. During the climb PX4's nav_state is NAVIGATION_STATE_AUTO_TAKEOFF, which is already not AUTO_LOITER — so the cell is reachable by timing alone. MIS_TAKEOFF_ALT is raised to 40 m to widen that window from under 2 s (the 2.5 m default) to roughly 25 s at PX4's default climb rate, so the 6 s delay lands mid-climb with margin either side. Raising the param avoids passing an explicit NAV_TAKEOFF altitude, which PX4 reads as AMSL — the lab's Zurich home sits near 488 m, so a literal 40 would be underground.

SOURCE HYPOTHESIS (PX4 Navigator::run, DO_REPOSITION):
  - applies the setpoint only if ((uint32_t)cmd.param2 & 1) != 0  (CHANGE_MODE), OR
    nav_state is already NAVIGATION_STATE_AUTO_LOITER
  - and in either case only while ARMING_STATE_ARMED
Flag clear + AUTO_TAKEOFF satisfies neither branch, so the prediction is that PX4 does NOT apply the setpoint.

OPEN: whether PX4 answers with a non-ACCEPTED MAV_RESULT or says nothing. Both are publishable, so both PASS. The mavlink receiver may ack before Navigator ever sees the command, in which case an ACCEPTED ack with no change of course is itself the finding — say so explicitly. Only a send that never reached the wire measures nothing and fails the run.

WHAT THE RIG SHOULD RECORD:
1. param status — did MIS_TAKEOFF_ALT=40 take? (if not, the climb window is ~2 s and the reposition almost certainly arrived in AUTO_LOITER, which measures the wrong cell)
2. takeoff status, and whether the vehicle was still climbing when the reposition went out
3. reposition status — result, detail, resultCode, or a 10 s timeout, which is a real answer here
4. Whether the vehicle turned toward the target or kept climbing to 40 m
